final_text:
Out of the 10 expected species, 7 were called present, and 1 species was called that isn't in the mock.

I used only the species rows (rank code S): there are 20, with 237,500 clade reads in total. I converted each count to a percent of that total, compared names in lowercase with the single Lactobacillus fermentum rename, and counted a species as present at 0.1% or more.

| Species (as reported) | Clade reads | % of species reads | Called? | Expected? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| limosilactobacillus fermentum (= Lactobacillus fermentum) | 146,108 | 61.52 | yes | yes |
| bacillus spizizenii | 37,874 | 15.95 | yes | **no** |
| enterococcus faecalis | 34,730 | 14.62 | yes | yes |
| pseudomonas aeruginosa | 9,018 | 3.80 | yes | yes |
| staphylococcus aureus | 3,591 | 1.51 | yes | yes |
| salmonella enterica | 3,072 | 1.29 | yes | yes |
| escherichia coli | 2,191 | 0.92 | yes | yes |
| listeria monocytogenes | 811 | 0.34 | yes | yes |
| bacillus subtilis | 2 | 0.0008 | no | yes |
| (11 other species) | ≤41 each | <0.02 | no | no |

- **Expected but not called:** bacillus subtilis has only 2 reads. Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Cryptococcus neoformans have no species rows in the report at all.
- **Called but not expected:** bacillus spizizenii, at 15.9%. It used to be classified as a subspecies of B. subtilis, so the database probably assigned the B. subtilis reads to it. The rules allow only the fermentum rename, so I counted it as a separate, unexpected species.
